newsitem.title: USA: American Greetings calls off merger with Foster Grant.
newsitem.headline: American Greetings calls off merger with Foster Grant.

text.p: American Greetings Corp. said Tuesday it has called off its planned $50 million purchase of the Foster Grant Group from BEC Group Inc.

"We have decided that going forward with this acquisition at this time does not fit with our business objectives," said Erwin Weiss, senior vice president of American Greetings' consumer products division.
The Cleveland-based greeting card company said in August it would buy the moderately-priced sunglass division from the BEC Group Inc. The selling price was $50 million.

"We were unable to agree on philosophies and price with American Greetings," BEC said. "As a result, we are returning to the management-led buyout of Foster Grant that we had originally intended prior to the American Greetings offer."

BEC Group, an optical technologies company based in Rye, N.Y., said it expects to close the sale of Foster Grant, which has annual sales of about $90 million, before the release of its third-quarter results. Its third quarter ends Sept. 30.
BEC Group stock was down 12 cents to $4.87 on the New York Stock Exchange. American Greetings stock rose 12 cents to $28.37 on the American Stock Exchange.
